### MEDIUM: Installer persistently binds the provider to whatever coordinator URL served the installer script
[coordinator/api/install\.sh:598](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/7337d9bdc86112377b6c9813de1ce66d689a937b/coordinator/api/install.sh#L598) · A-008, T-040

The installer now writes COORD\_URL into \~/\.config/darkbloom/provider\.toml as \[coordinator\] url\. Before this change COORD\_URL only chose the download source for that one install run\. It now decides where the provider connects on every later start, login and update, and where it sends its provider token and registration\. COORD\_URL is the \`\_\_DARKBLOOM\_COORD\_URL\_\_\` template value, or the caller's COORD\_URL environment variable\. Per T\-040, the template value can come from the request Host / X\-Forwarded\-Proto headers when baseURL is not configured\. Validation \(\`provider\_websocket\_url\`\) only checks character syntax; any https host passes\. A poisoned installer \(Host\-header injection with a shared cache, a \`COORD\_URL=\` one\-liner from a phishing page, or a malicious mirror\) would leave the Mac permanently pointed at an attacker coordinator\. That coordinator would see the provider's API token and the inference traffic routed to it, while the provider still looks legitimate locally\. The signed\-binary designated\-requirement check blocks a swapped binary but not this config change\. Fix: allow a non\-production URL only when a first\-party allowlist matches or the user passes an explicit flag\. Also have the provider confirm non\-default coordinators interactively, and make sure the coordinator never derives the embedded COORD\_URL from request headers\.
